title: Connecting Applications to Hybrid Tables
author: Adam Timm
universal_best_practices: Use bound variables (prepared statements) for all queries — enables plan cache reuse
Use connection pooling with long-lived connections — eliminates 100-500ms reconnect overhead
Use private key (JWT) authentication for service accounts
Colocate application in same cloud region as Snowflake account
Keep AUTOCOMMIT = TRUE (default) for OLTP workloads — also required to call an Inline Stored Procedure, which cannot run inside an open transaction
Never benchmark HT latency via Snowsight — always use application driver

jdbc.call_inline_procedure: prepareStatement("CALL proc(?, ?)") + executeQuery(); the result set has one row and one column named after the procedure, read with rs.getString(1)
jdbc.pool: HikariCP — set maxLifetime and net.snowflake.jdbc.ttl to same value
jdbc.kafka_pattern: Kafka consumer (batched=true, concurrency=partitions) -> HikariCP pool -> executeBatch -> HT

python.call_inline_procedure: cursor.execute("CALL proc(?, ?)", (arg1, arg2)) then cursor.fetchone()[0] for a scalar RETURNS, or fetchall() for RETURNS TABLE
python.binding_syntax: ? (qmark) — do NOT use f-strings or %s formatting
python.pool: SQLAlchemy create_engine with pool_size, pool_pre_ping=True, pool_recycle=1800

nodejs.call_inline_procedure: connection.execute({ sqlText: 'CALL proc(?, ?)', binds: [arg1, arg2] }); the scalar result is rows[0].PROC_NAME, uppercased
nodejs.binding_syntax: ? or :N positional — never string template literals
nodejs.pool_warning: Default evictionRunIntervalMillis=0 disables eviction — always set it

snowpark.bulk_pattern: session.sql('INSERT INTO ht SELECT ... FROM staging WHERE batch_id = ?').bind([id])

inline_stored_procedures.purpose: Execute a multi-statement unit of work atomically against hybrid tables with less per-statement overhead than a standard stored procedure.
inline_stored_procedures.mechanism: The body is compiled as a single unit and pushed down to the query processing layer, avoiding the per-statement round trips of a standard stored procedure.
inline_stored_procedures.syntax: CREATE OR REPLACE INLINE PROCEDURE name(arg TYPE) RETURNS TYPE LANGUAGE SQL AS $$ BEGIN ATOMIC ... END $$;
inline_stored_procedures.call: CALL is an ordinary SQL statement, so every driver invokes it with its normal bind syntax. No driver-specific API and no minimum driver version beyond the versions already required for hybrid tables.
inline_stored_procedures.argument_reference: Reference arguments inside the body with a colon prefix, for example :p_order_id.
inline_stored_procedures.autocommit_required: Cannot be invoked from inside an open transaction; must be called with autocommit enabled. Commit or roll back before calling.
inline_stored_procedures.compiled_at_call_time: Compilation happens at CALL time, not CREATE time, so CREATE can succeed while the first CALL fails on an unsupported construct. Call each new procedure once in a test environment.

returns.scalar: RETURNS <type> yields a single-row, single-column result set whose column is named after the procedure.
returns.table: RETURNS TABLE(...) yields a normal result set; declared column types must match the query's types exactly.

inline_stored_procedures.error_propagation: An unhandled failure inside the body propagates to the driver as a normal statement error and rolls back every earlier change in the same call. The code is the failing statement's own code, not a single procedure-level code: duplicate primary key surfaces as 200001, division by zero as 100051, a NOT NULL violation as 391467. Match on the driver's exception type rather than one code.
inline_stored_procedures.exception_handler_tradeoff: An EXCEPTION handler inside the procedure returns a controlled value instead of rolling back, which commits statements that already succeeded in that call and can leave partial state. Omit the handler and handle the error in application code when all-or-nothing behavior is required.
key_constraints: No dynamic context functions: CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIME, CURRENT_DATE, SYSDATE, SYSTIMESTAMP, GETDATE, LOCALTIME, LOCALTIMESTAMP (error 090277). Compute the value in the caller and pass it as an argument.
No DDL, no dynamic SQL (EXECUTE IMMEDIATE), no nested stored procedure calls, no nested atomic blocks
No explicit BEGIN, COMMIT, or ROLLBACK inside the body
Owner's rights only; no session variables; at most one database referenced per body
Not a bulk-loading path; use batch inserts or COPY INTO for ingest
inline_stored_procedures.when_not_to_use: A single-statement write is faster as direct DML with bound variables; wrapping one statement adds no benefit.

anti_patterns.name: String literals in queries
anti_patterns.impact: Disables plan cache, 10-100ms extra compilation per query

anti_patterns.name: Single-row inserts in a loop
anti_patterns.impact: N round-trips for N rows; use batch APIs instead

anti_patterns.name: Oversized connection pool
anti_patterns.impact: Warehouse queuing; match pool size to warehouse concurrency

anti_patterns.name: Benchmarking via Snowsight
anti_patterns.impact: 5-20x higher latency than driver; not representative

anti_patterns.name: Inconsistent schema qualification
anti_patterns.impact: Splits plan cache into multiple entries; reduces hit rate

anti_patterns.name: Calling an Inline Stored Procedure with autocommit disabled
anti_patterns.impact: The call fails; Inline Stored Procedures cannot run inside an open transaction

anti_patterns.name: Adding an EXCEPTION handler to a multi-statement Inline Stored Procedure that needs atomicity
anti_patterns.impact: Handling the error commits statements that already succeeded, leaving partial state instead of rolling back

anti_patterns.name: Calling CURRENT_TIMESTAMP inside an Inline Stored Procedure body
anti_patterns.impact: Fails at CALL time with error 090277; pass the value as an argument instead
